messages:
Maya (Support): FYI escalating — customer 'FinData' reporting lots of 429s starting ~09:10 UTC after we began the new rate-limit rollout for text-generation. They pasted a sample response header: 

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 169
{ "error": "rate_limit_exceeded" }

Their app traffic is bursty (lots of short lived sessions). They said the previous limits worked fine. Opening thread so eng + product can decide rollback/canary adjustments.

Omar (SRE): thanks, looking. Do we have rollout config ID? Maya can you paste link to feature flag or rollout dashboard? Also any repro traffic pattern would help (one API key vs many).

Maya (Support): Rollout config: https://console.redwood/test-rollouts/rl-policy-2026-v2 (canary=20% at 09:00 UTC). Customer uses a single API key for many end-users. Repro: they hit generation endpoint with parallel requests (100-300/s) in short bursts for 2–3s windows.

Priya (Product): 20% canary of the policy was supposed to apply per-customer namespace, but behavior might be per-route. If single API key counts as one 'source' then token-bucket refill might be too slow for bursts. Our canary objective was to measure infra impact; we didn't intend to throttle customer-visible bursts that much. Suggest immediate pause. Rollback threshold: >5% of _active_ customers getting 429 within 30m => rollback. Current alerting shows FinData + 2 others.

RateLimit-Bot: [automated alert] rate_limit.policy.v2.canary: error-rate spike: 429s increased to 6.1% (baseline 0.3%) across canary cohort in last 15m. Canary cohort size=21% of traffic.

Omar (SRE): I see elevated 429s and corresponding token-bucket depletion in the metrics. Key finding: the new policy reduced burst capacity by lowering the burst_size parameter from 200 to 20 for this route. That was deliberate to reduce peak CPU, but for single-key multi-client customers it kills them.

Ken (Eng-Platform): if we agree to pause we can toggle the rollout flag to rollback to previous policy in <2min. Command (admin API):

```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/internal/rollouts/rl-policy-2026-v2/rollback \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \n  -d '{"target": "previous", "reason": "support-escalation: excessive 429s"}'
```

I'll stand by to execute once we have thumbs. We should also consider a hotfix that keeps burst_size higher for API-key scope while limiting overall qps.

Alex (Billing): heads-up — if we rollback we might need to offer credits to affected customers. FinData already opened a billing case saying users lost paid workflows. If rollback doesn't fully mitigate (some requests failed and charged), we may need to adjust invoices. I'll coordinate post-incident.

Lina (Customer Success): I've got a draft reply: 

"Thanks for flagging this — we're pausing the recent rate-limit change and investigating. Short-lived bursts from a single API key are being temporarily restored to previous behavior. We'll follow up with timeline and any account credits." 

Maya (Support): +1. Customer asked for repro steps they can run to confirm fix. Suggested repro (to share):

```
# simulate burst from single api key
for i in {1..300}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood/generate &
done; wait
```

Omar (SRE): I ran internal replay of FinData's sample traffic against canary policy and reproduced the 429 spike. Root cause: burst_size param change + per-key global rate calculation that doesn't consider ephemeral client fan-out. Patch options:
- quick rollback to previous policy (safest)
- hotfix: increase burst_size only for api-key scope, leave global cpu caps in place (more targeted)

Priya (Product): Given customer impact, let's rollback the rollout for now and schedule a controlled hotfix in next patch. Rollback criteria satisfied (multiple paying customers affected). Also request post-mortem and a tweak to canary targeting rules (exclude single-key high-fanout accounts or apply per-session bucket).

Ken (Eng-Platform): executing rollback now. Running the curl above with admin token.

deploy-bot: Deploy request accepted: rollout rl-policy-2026-v2 -> rollback to previous at 2024-07-21T09:28:12Z by Ken.

RateLimit-Bot: [info] rollback completed. Canary cohort now back to previous policy. 429s dropping in last 60s.

Omar (SRE): 429s for FinData dropped to baseline in our replay and in customer logs. We'll keep extra monitoring for next 2 hours. Adding temporary dashboard: per-api-key burst_fill, token_bucket_size, per-route qps.

Maya (Support): Sending update to customer now. Copy of message: 

"We paused the recent rate-limit update that caused your requests to be throttled. You should see normal behavior within minutes. We're following up with a technical post-mortem and will offer credits if needed. If you still see 429s, please run the attached repro and paste logs. — Maya, Support"

Lina (Customer Success): Customer confirmed restored behavior ~09:35 UTC, says workflows resumed. Asking for timeline and compensation.

Alex (Billing): I'll prepare a credit proposal draft; please collect failed request counts for FinData (support ticket id SD-9832).

Priya (Product): Action items: 1) post-mortem (owner: Omar) 2) change canary rules to exclude single-key high-fanout accounts (owner: Priya) 3) implement hotfix to keep per-key burst_size larger (owner: Ken) 4) update rollout runbook to include real-time 429 thresholds and automatic rollback (owner: Product + SRE).

Omar (SRE): I'll take post-mortem. Early notes: add synthetic tests that simulate single-key fanout bursts during canary. Also capture X-RateLimit-* headers in customer-facing errors to help debugging.

Maya (Support): closing loop — customer happy with rollback and awaiting credits & post-mortem. Will re-open if anything else pops. Thanks all :thumbsup:
